title: Woman charged after newborn found dead in wooded area in Halifax released on bail
summary: Ramandeep Kaur faces charges including disposing of the body of a child with the intent to conceal the fact it had been delivered, offering an indignity to a dead body.

image.caption: Ramandeep Kaur, 27, appeared in Halifax provincial court on Thursday. She was released on bail with conditions. (Craig Paisley/CBC)

blocks.text: Ramandeep Kaur faces charges including disposing of the body of a child with the intent to conceal the fact it had been delivered, offering an indignity to a dead body.
Ramandeep Kaur faces charges including offering an indignity to a dead body
A woman who was charged after a newborn was found dead in a wooded area in Halifax this spring has been released on bail.
Ramandeep Kaur, 27, appeared in Halifax provincial court on Thursday morning to seek release on bail.
Kaur, wearing a red sweatshirt that said "perfectionist," participated in the court proceedings with assistance from a Punjabi interpreter.

Judge Marc Chisholm granted Kaur's release on conditions that she reside with her surety at an address in Halifax, that she remain in Nova Scotia, that she report to Halifax Regional Police in person each week, that she attend court when directed, and that she deposit her passport and Indian national identity card. The court also ordered a $1,000 promise to pay for both Kaur and her surety.
The conditions were agreed upon by the Crown, Kevin Nightingale, and Kaur's lawyer, Trevor McGuigan.

Kaur and her husband, Sukhpreet Singh, 24, are charged with disposing of the body of a child with the intent to conceal the fact it had been delivered, two counts of obstruction by lying, including to a police officer, and offering an indignity to a dead body.

Defence awaits evidence in case of newborn baby whose remains were found near Halifax

blocks.text: On May 22, a 23-year-old woman who had recently given birth was admitted to the hospital in critical condition, but the baby was not with her.
Police conducted an extensive search, and the remains of the infant were found off Old Coach Road in Goodwood, N.S., two days later.
On May 27, the baby’s mother — a relative of Singh’s — died in hospital. Police have said it appeared her condition when she was admitted was a medical one and not the result of violence.
A spokesperson for Halifax Regional Police said Thursday it will likely be a few more months before police get results from the medical examiner's office on the cause of the baby's death.
Kaur and Singh are scheduled to appear in Halifax provincial court on Oct. 14.
